title: UC6 Build Order — empty repo to M3
question: In what order do I build this from nothing, and what proves each step is done?
scope: Sequenced by Phase only (Phase 0–5, docs/milestones.md §2). Milestone (M1/M2/M3) and Stage (A/B/C) are the other two axes and are shown as labels, never as sequence — they are three separate axes and must not be conflated (CONTEXT.md §2).

nodes.label: Standardise the environment and pin the distro

card.builds: Ubuntu on every team member's machine (dual-boot expected, WSL2 only as a per-person accommodation whose results do not count toward a gate), then the ROS 2 distro and tutorial commit/tag pinned by reading the tutorial repository itself rather than assuming.
creates: An Ubuntu LTS partition per machine, paired to the pinned ROS 2 distro
Unity Editor for Linux, running the Unity Robotics Hub tutorial scene
Status updates recorded into ADR-003 and ADR-007 (status change, not new ADRs)
card.gate: Phase 0 exit gate: tutorial repo runs unmodified; ROS 2 distro pinned (ADR-003 finalised); Unity version confirmed; TurtleBot3 Waffle Pi model/plugin availability confirmed.
card.scenario: No scenario yet — Phase 0 is verified by its exit gate alone; the scenario matrix starts at S-00 in Phase 1.
card.why_first: ADR-007 is upstream of every other Phase 0 task: the distro cannot be verified against the tutorial repo until an Ubuntu environment exists.

card.builds: MySQL under docker-compose with docs/schema.sql applied on container init, dry-run on every team member's machine.
creates: docker-compose configuration mounting docs/schema.sql into /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/
The six tables from docs/schema.sql: categories, items, shelf_slots, tasks, runs, run_events
card.gate: Phase 0 exit gate: docker-compose up succeeds with docs/schema.sql applied, on every member's machine.
card.scenario: No scenario yet — verified by the Phase 0 exit gate. The seeded catalog it produces is later shown as step 1 of the grading-day demo (test-plan.md §5).
card.why_first: Phase 1's own exit gate requires the orchestrator skeleton to be operational against a seeded MySQL, so the schema has to exist before the skeleton does.

nodes.label: Adapt the tutorial scene and fix the bridge contract

card.builds: The Unity warehouse scene adapted from the Unity Robotics Hub Nav2 + SLAM example, plus the C# side of the bridge and the custom message set the rest of the system references.
creates: Unity warehouse scene with shelf and drop-off poses matching the seeded shelf_slots grid
Robot Controller (C#), ROS-TCP-Connector configuration
Item Re-parent / Release Handler (C#) — dwell-then-re-parent, release at drop-off
warehouse_msgs / warehouse_srvs: PickupEvent, PickupAck, PlaceEvent, PlaceAck, CollisionEvent, ReplanEvent, ClearanceSample, CategoryUpdate, TaskResult, GetNextTask, SetCategory
The M1 map produced by the SLAM/mapping step, used as the global costmap static_layer
card.gate: Contributes to the Phase 1 exit gate (S-00 below). Its own blocking check is the architecture.md §2 [VERIFY]: confirm the tutorial's actual default topic set before the contract is frozen.
card.scenario: S-00 — open room, no obstacles, single robot, Standard category only.
card.why_first: The bridge contract is referenced by every ROS 2 node built afterwards; changing it later invalidates work in all four owner areas.

card.builds: The episode spine: the single database-touching node, and the per-task FSM that drives two legs with a dwell at each end.
creates: task_manager (Python): /task_manager/get_next_task service, the episode-end transaction, and the FR-16 disk-buffer fallback
mission_orchestrator (Python): shelf leg → dwell → profile → drop-off leg → dwell → report, over /navigate_to_pose
The seed script (data-model.md §5): three categories rows, a shelf_slots grid, a sample items catalog, a pending tasks queue
card.gate: Phase 1 exit gate: S-00 goal success rate ≥ 90% over N=20 and 0 collisions; task_manager / mission_orchestrator skeleton operational against seeded MySQL.
card.scenario: S-00 — open room, no obstacles, single robot, Standard category only.
card.why_first: NFR-03 is cheapest to hold from the first line: exactly one node performs database I/O, so no control-loop node ever acquires a query to remove later.

card.builds: The measurement path, without which no gate from here on can be evaluated: in-run event accumulation plus the harness that repeats a scenario N≥20 times and exports CSV.
creates: metrics_collector (Python): collision, replan, clearance_sample and goal_outcome events; the per-episode run summary on /task/next_task_result
Headless runner parameterised by scenario_id and run_count (default 20)
CSV exporter: <scenario_id>_results.csv (16 columns) and <scenario_id>_summary.csv
card.gate: Phase 1 exit gate, measured: S-00 goal success rate ≥ 90% over N=20 with 0 collisions — a number that cannot be produced without this node and this runner.
card.scenario: S-00 — and every scenario after it, since the runner is what makes N≥20 per scenario practical within 8 weeks.
card.sequencing_note: Phase placement inferred, not stated: milestones.md §2 names the Phase 1 exit gate as a numeric rate over N=20, and milestones.md §1 assigns metrics_collector, the headless runner and CSV export to the Integration/Test Lead. The Phase 5 exit gate governs the completed CSV evidence set, not the tool's first build.

nodes.label: Static obstacle avoidance: costmaps and planner tuning

card.builds: The first graded capability. Nav2 is configured, never rebuilt: the obstacle layer is enabled for static obstacles, the global planner is tuned for costmap responsiveness, and stock recovery behaviours are left at defaults.
creates: Nav2 YAML parameter layers over the tutorial defaults (no Nav2 source modified)
global_costmap: static_layer from the M1 map, obstacle_layer from /scan, inflation_layer
local_costmap: rolling-window obstacle_layer from /scan, inflation_layer
Unity scenes for the three static scenarios, including a 1.5× footprint corridor and a dead-end branch
card.gate: S-01 and S-02: 0 collisions across 20 consecutive runs, min clearance ≥ 0.15 m; S-02 additionally path length ratio ≤ 1.3. S-03: 0 collisions across 20 consecutive runs and goal success rate ≥ 90% over N=20, with recovery resolving the dead end rather than merely avoiding contact.
card.scenario: S-01 static-only · S-02 narrow corridor · S-03 dead-end recovery.

nodes.label: Wire the category to the motion profile

card.builds: motion_profile_node and the parameter path it drives — end to end, even while only the Standard profile is exercised.
creates: motion_profile_node (Python): /mission/active_category subscriber, /motion_profile/set_category service
Category parameter sets: Standard 0.26 / 2.5 / 0.30, Fragile 0.10 / 2.5 / 0.50, Heavy 0.15 / 1.0 / 0.35 (max_vel_x / acc_lim_x / inflation_radius)
The fail-safe path: on service failure or timeout, hold Fragile values and log a warning run_event
card.gate: Phase 2 exit gate: category profile mechanism wired end-to-end, even with only the Standard profile exercised — alongside the S-01–S-03 numbers above.
card.scenario: S-01–S-03 for the phase gate; the mechanism's own numeric proof is S-06, run in Phase 3.
card.framing: A mechanism reinforcing obstacle avoidance, never a standalone feature (PRD G4). Category is a catalog attribute, never inferred (ADR-002).

nodes.label: Dynamic avoidance and the ADR-004 benchmark

card.builds: The graded headline. Scripted NPC obstacles in Unity, the local costmap driving short-horizon avoidance, tightened recovery timeouts to keep replans responsive, and the pre-registered DWB-vs-TEB selection.
creates: Scripted NPC Obstacle Controllers (C#) crossing the path at a fixed interval
Two local-planner parameter files (DWB and TEB) kept buildable until the benchmark decides
Costmap obstacle layers extended to LIDAR-observed dynamic obstacles; tuned spin / back-up / wait timeouts
The replan hook publishing /metrics/replan_event
card.gate: S-04: goal success rate ≥ 85% over N=20, ≤ 1 collision per 20 runs, replan count > 0 on at least 1 run in 20. Benchmark criterion, pre-registered: the configuration with the lower collision count over N=20 in S-04 is adopted; on a tie, the higher goal success rate; time-boxed to 2 days, defaulting to DWB if inconclusive.

card.builds: The numeric evidence that the category mechanism measurably changes robot behaviour — a fixed route in an open room, run 20 times per category.
creates: The S-06 fixed-route scene and its three 20-run task batches (60 runs total)
The cross-run mean-linear-velocity-per-category rollup in the CSV exporter (not a per-run runs column)
card.gate: S-06: mean linear velocity per category strictly ordered Fragile < Heavy < Standard, with each pairwise difference ≥ 0.03 m/s. Closes the Phase 3 exit gate together with S-04 and the finalised local planner.
card.scenario: S-06 — per-category profile, ungraded but proves FR-09.

nodes.label: Harden, produce the evidence, rehearse the demo

card.builds: The submission. Stage A alone is sufficient to enter this phase and to ship.
creates: N≥20 CSV-exported runs per required scenario, from the headless runner
<scenario_id>_results.csv and <scenario_id>_summary.csv for S-00 through S-06
The 9-step scripted manual demo sequence, plus pre-recorded headless logs as the grading-day fallback
Finalised documentation and the packaged submission
card.gate: Phase 5 exit gate: headless runner has produced N≥20 CSV-exported runs per required scenario; manual demo sequence rehearsed at least twice; documentation finalised; submission packaged. Entry gate: Phase 3 exit met — Stage A is sufficient.
card.scenario: S-00 through S-06, replayed as the evidence set; the live demo runs S-02, S-04 and S-06.

nodes.label: Stage B / Stage C multi-robot — gated stretch
nodes.milestone: Beyond M3 — never required for a graded milestone

card.builds: One independently-navigating second robot (Stage B), then a third (Stage C) — each a full Nav2 stack under its own namespace and TF prefix, entered only if the prior stage's exit gate is met.
creates: Per-robot namespaces /robot1…/robot3 and TF prefixes robot1/…robot3/, with a single shared map frame [VERIFY]
A resolution of the ROS-TCP-Endpoint question: one endpoint multiplexed, or one endpoint process per robot on incrementing ports (e.g. 10000+n), load-tested before Stage B
card.gate: Stage B gate: 2 robots run without TF/namespace conflict across 20 consecutive runs in S-05, and goal success rate ≥ 80% over N=20 for every robot in the stage. Stage C gate: the same with 3 robots, attempted only within remaining Week 7 time. If either gate fails, ship the prior stage.
card.scenario: S-05 — multi-robot, explicitly beyond M3 and gated.
card.warning: This is a terminal branch, not a step on the way to M3. Stage A is the M3 baseline and already satisfies every graded milestone; Phase 4 is attempted only after the Phase 3 exit gate is met, and its failure costs nothing but the stretch. A namespace conflict here is a namespace conflict, never a collision.

edges.label: Phase 0 exit gate met → Phase 1 entry
Phase 1 exit gate met (S-00) → Phase 2 entry
Phase 2 exit gate met → Phase 3 entry
Phase 3 exit gate met — Stage A is sufficient to ship
only if the Phase 3 exit gate is met, and only as time permits (ADR-006)

Not a build step; the two risks that actually move the order (tutorial/distro drift, benchmark overrun) are carried in the s1 and s8 cards.
Gated behind the M3/Stage exit gates, never on the graded path, and not part of any phase exit gate.

omitted.why: Collapsed into one terminal gated-stretch node; C is entered only if B's gate passes, and neither is required for a graded milestone.
